questions.q: What does the CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES environment variable control?
options: The precision format used for training
The NCCL backend version
The number of CPU threads available to PyTorch
Which physical GPUs a process can see and use
questions.explain: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES restricts which physical GPUs are visible to a process, remapping them internally starting from device 0.

questions.q: What is the main architectural downside of torch.nn.DataParallel?
options: It requires manually writing CUDA kernels
It cannot run on more than one GPU at all
It only works with CPU tensors
It runs in a single process and funnels gradient-gathering through one GPU, creating a bottleneck that doesn't scale across nodes
questions.explain: DataParallel operates in a single process, splitting batches across GPUs but gathering gradients back onto one GPU, which becomes a bottleneck and prevents scaling beyond a single node.

questions.q: How does DistributedDataParallel (DDP) avoid the bottleneck that DataParallel has?
options: By only training on one GPU and ignoring the rest
By running the entire model on the CPU instead
By running one separate process per GPU, each with its own model copy, and synchronizing gradients across processes without a single gathering point
By avoiding gradient computation entirely
questions.explain: DDP runs one process per GPU, each with its own full copy of the model. After backward(), gradients are synchronized (via NCCL) and averaged across all processes without any single GPU acting as a bottleneck.

It compiles the script into CUDA C++
It starts 4 separate Python processes, one per GPU, each receiving a LOCAL_RANK value

questions.explain: torchrun launches one process per GPU (4 in this case), with each process receiving a LOCAL_RANK environment variable telling it which GPU it owns.

questions.q: What does the LOCAL_RANK environment variable tell a DDP training process?
options: The total number of nodes in the training cluster
Which GPU, on the current machine, that process should use
The current training epoch number
The batch size for that process
questions.explain: LOCAL_RANK identifies which GPU on the current machine a given DDP process is responsible for, set automatically by the launcher (such as torchrun).
